title: Know Your Nafs Quiz
description: Questions about the concept of the nafs, its stages, and ways to discipline it.

questions.question: Which is the most accurate definition of the nafs?
options: It is an independent evil entity that must be destroyed.
It is only an impulse that leads to evil.
It is a broad concept relating to a person's inner self, desires, inclinations, and sphere of responsibility.
It refers only to bodily needs.
questions.explanation: The nafs is our inner self, which must not be destroyed but purified, disciplined, and directed toward Allah's pleasure.

questions.question: What is the main goal regarding the nafs?
options: To purify and discipline the nafs and direct it toward Allah's pleasure
To suppress the nafs completely
To deny the existence of the nafs
To fulfill every desire of the nafs
questions.explanation: The nafs exists not to be destroyed, but to be purified and directed toward Allah.

questions.question: What is the fundamental Quranic principle concerning the nafs as capable of inclining toward both good and evil?
options: A person cannot attain salvation without struggling against the nafs.
The nafs can be controlled only by strong people.
The evil side of the nafs must be completely suppressed.
Purifying the nafs brings success, while corrupting it brings loss.
questions.explanation: Purifying the nafs brings success, while corrupting it brings loss. Human beings were created with these two inclinations.

questions.question: How is the heading 'Raw Nafs' presented?
options: As a required stage explicitly mentioned in the Quran
As an educational heading that gives beginners an introduction
As the first stage of the classical seven-stage classification
As a technical term used in Sufi literature
questions.explanation: Raw Nafs is not part of the classical classification; it is an instructional heading added to provide an accessible introduction for users unfamiliar with the subject.

questions.question: What is the defining feature of the raw nafs?
options: An inner state that constantly questions its desires
An awareness that leads one to perform every action for Allah's pleasure
A state of following desires without questioning them, with little inner direction
A state of being aware of sin but unable to stop
questions.explanation: The raw nafs represents an inner state that follows desires without questioning them or asking, 'Does this desire bring me closer to Allah?'

questions.question: What does a person in the Emmâre state typically do after making a mistake?
options: Commits the sin, then makes excuses and defends it
Admits the mistake and apologizes
Feels remorse and turns to repentance
Realizes the sin and weeps
questions.explanation: In the Emmâre state, a person not only commits a sin but also defends it, downplays it, and makes excuses.

questions.question: What is the clearest sign of the Nefs-i Emmâre state?
options: Feeling remorse for sins and repenting
Submitting only to external pressures
Making only minor mistakes
Not only committing a sin but also making excuses and justifications for it
questions.explanation: In the Emmâre state, a person not only makes a mistake but also defends it, downplays it, and makes excuses.

questions.question: Which is not among the main signs of the Emmâre state?
options: Pride
Feeling remorse for sin
Greed and envy
Putting desire before truth
questions.explanation: Remorse is a sign of Levvâme, not Emmâre. In the Emmâre state, a person defends sin and makes excuses.

questions.question: What is recommended as the first step in dealing with the Emmâre state?
options: Seeing the sin as greater than it is
Giving up all desires
Recognizing the aspect of the nafs that commands evil and turning to repentance
Being alone
questions.explanation: Recognizing Emmâre teaches a person to seek refuge in Allah's mercy instead of justifying themselves.

questions.question: Which behavior best describes the Levvâme state?
options: Feeling sincere remorse after a mistake and holding oneself accountable
Continuing to make mistakes without noticing them
Sinking deeper as one commits sins
Remaining indifferent to everything
questions.explanation: Levvâme is a state of inward self-examination, remorse, and self-reproach after a mistake.

questions.question: How should remorse in the Levvâme state be understood?
options: As the beginning of despair
As a sign of a flaw and weakness
As proof that the person can no longer attain salvation
As a sign of awakening, not downfall
questions.explanation: Levvâme is a sign of awakening, not downfall. If directed properly, remorse can lead to repentance and reform.

questions.question: What happens when the feeling of remorse is directed properly?
options: The person feels worthless and abandons worship
It leads to repentance, reform, and steadfastness on the right path
Sins are automatically never repeated
The person begins to condemn others as well
questions.explanation: If directed properly, remorse leads to repentance, reform, and steadfastness on the right path; it should not turn into excessive guilt.

questions.question: Which statement about the name Nefs-i Mülhime is correct?
options: It appears explicitly in the Quran as 'nefs-i mülhime'
It is a term found only in hadith
It does not appear as a name in the Quran; it is used in the ethical and Sufi tradition based on the expression of inspiration
It is one of the four major stages of the nafs
questions.explanation: The name Mülhime does not appear explicitly in the Quran; it is a name used in the Sufi and ethical tradition based on the inspiration of both good and evil to the nafs.

questions.question: What is the main thing to be mindful of in the Mülhime state?
options: Evaluating inner voices against the standards of the Quran and Sunnah
Accepting every thought that arises within as inspiration
Blindly following one's inner voice
Failing to distinguish between whisperings and inspiration
questions.explanation: Not every inner voice is accepted as true. A believer weighs thoughts that arise within against the standards of the Quran, Sunnah, and morality, and strengthens inclinations that call toward God-consciousness.

questions.question: Why is it important to distinguish between whisperings, base desires, and sound inclinations in the Mülhime state?
options: Because a person should never trust their own nafs
Because the nafs is considered completely purified in this state
Because supplication is meaningless in this state
Because blindly acting on everything that arises within is dangerous
questions.explanation: Not every inner voice is inspiration; it may also be whisperings or base desires. Therefore, it is essential to measure thoughts that arise within against the standards of the Quran and Sunnah.

questions.question: How does a person in the Mutmainne state respond during difficult times?
options: By ignoring the difficulty
By maintaining trust in Allah even when shaken
By renewing their iman after the difficulty has passed
By complaining and questioning at every hardship
questions.explanation: The Mutmainne state does not deny difficulties; a person can face them while maintaining trust in Allah.

questions.question: How is the peace of the Mutmainne state described?
options: The complete disappearance of all desires
The complete improvement of external circumstances
The heart learning to trust Allah
Never making a mistake
questions.explanation: The peace of Mutmainne is not the disappearance of desires; it is the heart learning to trust Allah. A person does not deny difficulties, but does not lose their way by forgetting their Lord.

questions.question: Which statement about the Mutmainne state is false?
options: A person in this state never struggles or feels sad
The heart has learned to trust Allah
There is steadfastness in worship
Resistance to sin has grown stronger
questions.explanation: The Mutmainne state does not mean that a person never feels sad or struggles; it describes a state in which one can maintain trust in Allah amid difficulties.

questions.question: How does a person in the state of Râzıye respond when faced with a severe trial?
options: They carry on by denying their situation
They find relief by submitting to oppression and remaining silent
They feel no pain and remain indifferent to everything
Even in pain, they maintain their trust in Allah and do not rebel
questions.explanation: Rıza is not the absence of pain; it is not losing trust in Allah amid pain.

questions.question: What does Rıza mean?
options: Feeling no pain at all
Not losing trust in Allah, even amid pain
Remaining silent about everything
Ignoring difficulties
questions.explanation: Rıza is not the absence of pain; it is not losing trust in Allah, even amid pain. Rıza encompasses patience, gratitude, and submission.

questions.question: Can the state of Rıza be interpreted as submitting to oppression or remaining silent in the face of injustice?
options: Yes, Rıza means accepting everything
Yes, oppression is also Allah's decree
No; Rıza is submission to Allah's decree, while the responsibility to uphold people's rights and justice remains
No, but nothing can be said about this
questions.explanation: Rıza is submission to Allah's decree; it is not submission to oppression. The responsibility to uphold people's rights and justice remains.

questions.question: Which sentence best describes the state of Marzıyye?
options: The servant aims to earn Allah's pleasure through sincerity and humility
The servant regards their salvation as certain because they have performed acts of worship
The servant shares their spiritual superiority with others
The servant has reached a state in which they no longer sin
questions.explanation: Marzıyye is the effort to place sincerity, humility, and Allah's pleasure at the center; it is not self-admiration.

questions.question: Which attitude is incompatible with the state of Marzıyye?
options: Sincerity and humility
Good character and compassion
Placing Allah's pleasure at the center
Declaring oneself a servant with whom Allah is certainly pleased
questions.explanation: The station of Marzıyye is not self-admiration or saying, 'Allah is certainly pleased with me'; it is the effort to place sincerity, humility, and Allah's pleasure at the center.

questions.question: In the state of Marzıyye, what is a believer expected to choose instead of relying on their deeds?
options: Abandoning worship
Continuing with humility and hope in Allah's mercy
Continuing in reliance on their deeds
Judging the worship of others
questions.explanation: The servant continues with humility and hope in Allah's mercy, rather than relying on their deeds; this is the essence of the state of Marzıyye.

questions.question: Which statement about Nefs-i Kâmile is correct?
options: In this state, a person no longer makes any mistakes
A person begins to see themselves as superior to others
As a person becomes purified, they feel their need for Allah more deeply
Once a person reaches this state, there is no longer any need to discipline the nafs
questions.explanation: The perfected nafs is not one that sees itself as flawless; it is one that feels its need for Allah more deeply as it becomes purified.

questions.question: How is the perfected nafs defined?
options: A nafs that never forgets its need for Allah
A nafs that makes no mistakes
A nafs completely freed from all its desires
A nafs that sees itself as flawless
questions.explanation: The perfected nafs is not one that sees itself as flawless; it is one that never forgets its need for Allah.

questions.question: What attitude could pose a danger in the state of Kâmile/Zekiyye?
options: Continually repenting
Continuing with humility
Avoiding hidden sins
Claiming spiritual superiority
questions.explanation: Kâmile/Zekiyye should not be interpreted in a way that leads a person to claim spiritual superiority; every stage is understood in the context of Allah's grace and the servant's effort.

questions.question: What is the first step in disciplining the nafs?
options: Performing a great deal of voluntary worship
Repentance
Being alone
Criticizing others
questions.explanation: Disciplining the nafs begins with repentance, continues with self-examination, and is strengthened by worship and good character.

questions.question: What is the fundamental pillar of disciplining the nafs?
options: Only increasing voluntary acts of worship
Only cutting off social relationships
Holding fast to obligations and avoiding what is forbidden
Only reading books
questions.explanation: Holding fast to obligations and avoiding what is forbidden are the foundation of disciplining the nafs; supplication, dhikr, patience, gratitude, and righteous company provide support.

questions.question: Which of the following is not among the things that strengthen the discipline of the nafs?
options: Focusing on the faults of others
Supplication and dhikr
Patience and gratitude
Righteous company
questions.explanation: Focusing on the faults of others does not strengthen the discipline of the nafs; it prevents a person from confronting their own faults.

questions.question: What kind of process is disciplining the nafs?
options: A task done once and then completed
Something that happens only during major acts of worship
An effort that can be started only in old age
A lifelong discipline of servitude renewed every day
questions.explanation: Disciplining the nafs is not completed all at once; it is a lifelong discipline of servitude renewed every day.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a practical question that can be used in daily self-examination of the nafs?
options: What did I do today for Allah's pleasure?
What did I gain from others today?
Did I violate anyone's rights today?
What should I repent for today?
questions.explanation: Self-examination of the nafs focuses on our inner life and our responsibility toward Allah; what one has gained from others is not a question for this self-examination.

questions.question: What can happen if remorse is misdirected in the state of Levvâme?
options: It turns into Mutmainne
It turns into repentance and reform
It can turn into despair and feelings of worthlessness
It does not cause a regression to Emmâre
questions.explanation: When directed properly, remorse turns into repentance and reform; when misdirected, it can lead to excessive guilt and despair.

questions.question: In the classical Sufi tradition, how many stages are used to classify the levels of the nafs?
questions.explanation: According to the majority of Sufis, the classical seven-stage classification is accepted: emmâre, levvâme, mülhime, mutmainne, râzıye, marzıyye, kâmile/zekiyye.

questions.question: What does the narration say about a person who struggles against their nafs?
options: This person is protected from every sin
This person is already saved
This person no longer needs to discipline their nafs
This person is a mujahid in the true sense
questions.explanation: It has been stated that a person who struggles against their own nafs is a mujahid in the true sense. Struggling against the nafs is regarded as a great effort of servitude.
